decisions.check_result: Re-read every cited line (app.py 33, 351, 569, 577, 603, 608; engine.py 69, 74, 78; actuator.py 59; backend/Dockerfile 25, which exists although the file lacks a trailing newline). analyze is async def and calls analyze_video, insert_event and dispatch_alerts inline with no to_thread or executor; analyze_video has no frame or time cap; dispatch_alerts sleeps 0.5 s per event and the MQTT publish can wait 5 s, with Telegram (notifier.py:61) up to 10 s; the image runs a single uvicorn worker. The source path is real and crosses a boundary: one authenticated resident's upload would monopolise the loop serving all communities' async work (WebSocket frames, /ingest, middleware). The proposed confirmation, however, rests on a runtime event-loop stall that was not and could not be observed (no execution in this run), and the deployed worker count is a deployment fact, so the candidate is demoted from confirmed to needs_validation with a bounded stub-based local plan and an owner check of the container command. No severity is assigned.

Confirmed from source that upload_too_big (app.py:180-186) reads only Content-Length, defaulting to '0', so a chunked request passes limitar_subidas (472-485); analyze takes an UploadFile, so the framework parses and spools the full multipart body before the handler's 200 MB counter (598), which only bounds the copy into UPLOAD_DIR. /ingest repeats the pattern (627, 632) behind an edge token. Caddyfile has no request_body limit and port 8000 is published directly. The impact (filling the shared host disk via the temporary spool during one long request) crosses from one resident to all tenants, but whether the unpinned Starlette/python-multipart build imposes a file-part limit, whether the proxy forwards unbounded chunked bodies, and the capacity/sharing of the spool filesystem are outside source and decisive. Kept needs_validation with an exact tmpfs-bounded local plan.

Verified ws_live (app.py:538-573) has no per-user/per-camera connection count or frame-rate limit; resolve_camera (cameras.py:149-162) only checks ownership; each frame goes through asyncio.to_thread (569) to _process_frame (527-535) and LiveSession.process takes the single process-wide infer_lock (engine.py:48, 133); pacing exists only in the client JS (index.html:761-772). /ingest (623), the /analyze session check (476) and WebSocket auth share the default executor, while sync def routes use anyio's separate pool, which narrows (but does not remove) the shared effect; the description was corrected to say so. The cross-tenant degradation of other users' live detection is plausible from source but its magnitude depends on host CPU count, inference latency and lock acquisition behaviour, and any upstream connection limits are deployment facts. Kept needs_validation with a stubbed-latency local fixture.

Verified analyze_video writes a full-resolution JPEG per MEDIO/ALTO event at most every event_cooldown_s (5 s) of video time with no frame cap (engine.py:85-95) and live sessions write one per event per session (engine.py:153, app.py:563) into the shared ./events bind mount (docker-compose.yml:20). A repository grep found no Python code deleting evidence files or referencing plans.storage_gb or v_user_storage (schema lines 13, 311); the only os.remove calls are for upload temp files. The schema-defined quota is an intended, unenforced control and disk exhaustion would affect other communities, so this is not mere hardening, but bytes written per upload and the host disk layout/cleanup are outside source and decisive. Kept needs_validation.
